Entities and columns in Mortise
Build the Mortise language so that entity blocks with typed columns and the published column settings parse into the model the diagram shows.

Diagram DOM contract
Render every entity, column and link with the published data attributes, roles and accessible names, and place each new entity in the next free grid cell by the published rule.

Editor keyboard rules
In the schema text editor, Tab inserts two spaces, Shift+Tab removes up to two leading spaces, Escape lets the next Tab move focus to the diagram, and the save shortcut opens the save-version dialog.

Live in-place updates
Typing updates the diagram, the error list and the DDL preview in place within the published parse delay, with no reload, no submit button and no lost caret or selection.

Entity entrance motion
An entity that appears after a parse fades and grows into place within the published range while its rows fill in one after another, and under reduced motion it appears in place at once.

Hero type-to-table demo
The landing page sample editor types the published sample once when it comes into view, building three linked entities in about six seconds before handing over to live editing, and under reduced motion it shows the final state at once.

Projects autosave and survive reload
An owner's typed schema is saved by the server without a save button, and after a reload and from the dashboard the same text and diagram are back.

Error format and messages
Every language error uses the published line-and-column format and the published message list, the same way in the editor, the check API and the import API.

Error order, cap and gutter markers
The error list shows errors sorted by line then column, at most 20 followed by a count of the rest, and every line with an error carries a gutter marker named after its line and message.

Last valid diagram while the text has errors
While the text has errors, the diagram keeps its last valid parse under the published out-of-date banner, and the banner and the error list clear within the parse delay once the text is valid.

Editor status announcements
After each parse, the editor status live region announces the error count and the first error's line and column in the published copy.

Published parser limits
Text over the byte limit, schemas over the entity or statement limits, and DDL over the statement or nesting limits stop with the published error inside the published time budget instead of hanging.

Choices
Choice blocks define enums that columns can use as types, defaults are checked against the choice's values, and duplicate values are reported.

Composite keys and indexes
Several key columns form one composite primary key and index lines form plain or unique indexes; both show in each column's key marker, and indexes naming a missing column are reported.

Diagram outline
A visually hidden diagram outline lists every choice, entity, link and group in text order, using the published item names for screen readers.

Links and cardinalities
Link lines and inline link settings join two columns with one of four cardinality tokens and show as connectors carrying the published cardinality value.

Canonical text
Everything Joinery writes into the text (drawn links, groups, renames through the diagram, imports and templates) follows the published canonical printing rules.

Drawn links write back one line
Dragging from a column handle to another column inserts exactly one canonical many-to-one link line after the owning entity's block and its existing link lines, and leaves every other byte unchanged.

Keyboard link drawing
A keyboard user starts a link on a focused column with L, chooses the target with arrow keys or Tab, and completes with Enter or cancels with Escape, and each step is announced in the published copy.

Write-back and connector motion
A written-back link line is typed in at the published rate while the new connector draws itself and its endpoint rows flash; under reduced motion the line appears in one step and the rows are highlighted without animation.

Moving entities never changes the text
Arrow keys move a focused entity one grid step (five with Shift) and pointer drags snap to the grid; positions are saved in the layout, survive reload and never change the text.

Groups
Grouping selected ungrouped entities writes one canonical group block at the end of the text with the chosen group colour, and ungrouping removes exactly that block.

Layout-only colours
Entity and group colours come from the published list of six names, are stored only in the layout and never change the text.

Renaming entities
Renaming through the diagram rewrites the entity's name and every reference to it and keeps its position, while renaming in the text gives the new name the next free cell.

Arrange
The arrange action moves every entity to the published grid cells in text order, gliding there within the published range, or jumping there under reduced motion.

PostgreSQL export
PostgreSQL export follows the published statement shapes, quoting, type mapping, enum types, and constraint and index names.

MySQL export and reported lowering
MySQL export follows the published statement shapes, quoting and type mapping, and records every lossy lowering, including identifiers shortened to fit the dialect's limit, as a note in the file.

Export order and determinism
Exports order tables by dependency with ties broken by name and break cycles with ALTER TABLE statements, and identical text always gives byte-identical files.

Exports confirmed in storage
An export becomes downloadable, and its Download link appears, only after object storage confirms the file under the published key; the download then works through the app until the published lifetime ends.

Storage outage
While object storage is down, editing keeps saving, exports and imports answer the published 503 with the diagram-is-safe copy, health and the status strip report the outage, and everything recovers without a restart once storage returns.

Supported DDL subset
Import accepts the published subset of PostgreSQL and MySQL statements, rejects everything else with published messages in the shared line-and-column format, and changes nothing on rejection.

Merge by table name
A merge import matches tables by exact name, replaces matched entities, adds new ones and reports every statement as added, merged, skipped or ambiguous, and repeating the import changes nothing.

Original DDL kept as submitted
Every successful import stores the submitted DDL byte for byte in object storage, and the owner can download exactly those bytes again.

Export and import round trip
Importing Joinery's own export of a schema gives back the same model for every construct, apart from the lossy lowerings that the export's notes report.

Numbered versions
Saving a named version snapshots the text and layout under the next gapless number, starting at 1, even when two saves arrive at the same moment.

Exact restore
Restoring version N brings back exactly its text, entity positions, and entity and group colours as a new numbered version, keeps every earlier version, and reaches everyone in the project live.

Version comparison
Comparing two versions lists the entities added, removed and changed between them in the published copy.

Share links and invitations
The owner creates view or edit links, optionally emailed through the mail provider, and an invitation is shown as sent only after the provider has accepted it.

View-only access
A view link or a viewer role shows the diagram and a read-only editor with edit controls hidden, and every write from such a caller is refused with the published 403.

Rotating, turning off and expiry
When a link is rotated, turned off or reaches its expiry instant on the server clock, the old URL immediately answers the generic not-found response, and anyone viewing through it sees the published notice.

Immediate role changes
Downgrading an editor to viewer or removing them takes effect on their next request, and their open session turns read-only or closes within the live delay.

Invitations during a mail outage
When mail is down, a newly created link still works and its invitation shows as failed in the published copy; sending again succeeds once mail is back, without a restart.

Live edits between people
An edit accepted from one person appears in every other open copy, in both text and diagram, within the published live delay, without a reload and without moving anyone's caret.

Presence
People who have the project open appear as presence chips with the published names, and a person who leaves disappears within the presence timeout.

Server order decides concurrent edits
The server applies edits in arrival order and merges an edit with an older base when the entity blocks it changed have not changed since; otherwise it refuses the edit with the published 409, so every client converges on the server text.

Conflict notice
A person whose edit was refused sees the published conflict alert naming the other person and the entity, and their editor shows the server text.

Published breakpoints
The phone, tablet and desktop workspace layouts appear exactly at the published viewport ranges, and no published viewport overflows sideways.

Touch pan, pinch and tap
On touch screens one finger pans the diagram, two fingers pinch-zoom within the published limits shown in the zoom status, and tapping an entity opens its detail sheet.

Reduced motion
With reduced motion requested, every entrance, glide, typed write-back, connector draw and flash shows its end state at once and works the same way, and no animation loops anywhere.

Sign-in with an emailed code
A person signs up or signs in with a six-digit code emailed through the mail provider; the code works once and expires after the published lifetime.

Dashboard
A signed-in person creates, opens and renames projects from the dashboard, which shows the published empty state when they have no projects and keeps projects across reloads.

Not found means not found
Any project, share, version, export or import the caller cannot open answers with the same not-found response and page as a missing one.

Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from the run manifest on the published port, and the health route answers as published.

Grading setup route
A setup route guarded by the grading key creates users with sessions, and projects with text, layout, versions, members and shares, and returns their ids.

One error order and shape
Every API error uses the published JSON shape, and errors are checked in the published order.

Dialog and menu keyboard rules
Every dialog and menu keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside itself, closes on Escape and returns focus to its opener, and published shortcuts work whichever control in their region has focus.

Published copy verbatim
Every string this brief prints in backticks is rendered and announced character for character.

Landing page
The landing page carries the pinned status strip, the dark nav with menus, the centred hero stack with its tally bubble and charcoal button, the working sample editor, the dialects strip, the alternating feature rows, the card grid and the import banner, all as described.

Visual language
Every screen uses the published palette roles, type, shapes and dark app-window islands on a white page, with AA contrast and comfortable tap targets.

Real services wiring
Credentials and URLs come only from the environment, provider-derived states come from real provider calls, and nothing fakes them in the browser or with a stub.
/app/run.json is a JSON object holding exactly the string fields install, build, serve and _schema set to run-manifest-v1.
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) with version and licence, plus the self-hosted fonts.
Every shipped package and font uses MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or BlueOak-1.0.0, or OFL-1.1 for fonts.
No datastore beyond PostgreSQL, MinIO and Mailpit is used: no SQLite, Redis, Valkey or files used as a database.
The committed package-lock.json drives install through npm ci.
The browser loads nothing from another origin; fonts, scripts, styles and images are served by the app.
The provided service configuration and its seeded development credentials stay unchanged.
